 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** **The correct match is:**

• **Ramanuja**

 
 
• He was born at Sriperumbudur.
 
• He was the disciple of Yamuna Muni and Vedprakash
 
• He founded the philosophy called **Vishishta Advaita** and preached Vaishnavism
 
• Kulottanga Chola who was a Shaivite banished Ramanujacharya for preaching Vaishnavism
 
• He wrote Sri Bashya and was the head of Srirangam Vaishnava Math
 
• Ramanujacharya preached Shudras and outcastes could also attain salvation by completely surrendering to the will of the guru.
 
• He was also referred to as Ilaya Perumalwhich means the radiant one.
 
• Ramanuja's chief contribution to philosophy was his insistence that discursive thought is necessary in humanity's search for the ultimate verities, that the phenomenal world is real and provides real knowledge, and that the exigencies of daily life are not detrimental or even contrary to the life of the spirit.
 
 
 
• **Madhavacharya**
 
 
• Shri Madhvacharya propounded **Dvaita philosophy** and spread his teachings all over India, twice during his lifetime.
 
• He composed more than 37 works in Sanskrit.
 
• 'Gita Thaathparya Nimaya' and 'Mahabharatha thaathpariya Nimaya' are his important works.
 
• He established eight Monasteries (Ashtamutts) at Udupi
 
 
 
• **Nimbaraka**
 
 
• Nimbarka, also called Nimbaditya or Niyamananda, (flourished 13th century, South India), Telugu-speaking Brahman, yogi, philosopher, and prominent astronomer who founded the devotional sect called Nimbarkas, Nimandi, or Nimavats, who worshipped the deity Krishna and his consort, Radha.
 
• Nimbarka has been identified with Bhaskara, a 9th- or 10th-century philosopher and celebrated commentator on the Brahma-sutras (Vedanta-sutras).
 
• Most historians of Hindu mysticism, however, hold that Nimbarka probably lived in the 12th or 13th century.
 
• The Nimbarka sect flourished in the 13th and 14th centuries in eastern India.
 
• Its philosophy held that men were trapped in physical bodies constricted by Prakriti (matter) and that only by surrendering to Radha-Krishna (not through their own efforts) could they attain the grace necessary for liberation from rebirth; then, at death, the physical body would drop away.
 
• **Dvaitadvaita Philosophy** of Nimbarka discusses three aspects of existence: Chit, achit, and Isvara. Chit and achit have Guna and Swabhaava which are different from those of Isvara. Isvara is independent while 'chit' and 'achit' have existence dependent upon the supreme.
 
• According to Nimbarka's Dvaitadvaita, Brahman is the highest reality. Brahman is a personal God. There is nothing equal or superior to him. Due to his greatness, nature, and qualities, he is known as Brahman. He is considered beyond any limit. Brahman is considered the sole cause of the creation, maintenance, and destruction of the Universe.
 
• Thus Nimbarka stressed bhakti-yoga, the yoga of devotion and faith.
 
• Many books were written about this once-popular cult, but most sources were destroyed by Muslims during the reign of the Mughal emperor Aurangzeb (1659–1707), and thus little information has survived about Nimbarka and his followers.
 
 
 
• **Vallabhacharya**
 
 
• Vallabhacharya propounded the **Sudhadvaita **Vedanta (Pure non-dualism) and a philosophy called Pustimarga (The path of Grace).
 
• He believed that Brahman is identified with Sri Krishna, characterized by Sat (Being), Cit (Consciousness) and Ananda (Bliss). Salvation is through Sneha (Deep-rooted love to God).

questions.question:
Arrange the following Mauryan Emperors in chronological order.

I. Bindusara

II. Brihadratha

III. Samprati

IV. Ashoka
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**I - IV - III - II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **chronological order** of the Mauryan Emperors mentioned in the question is as follows:
 
• **Bindusara**: He was the second emperor of the Mauryan Empire and the son of Chandragupta Maurya. His reign lasted from approximately 297 BCE to 273 BCE.
 
• **Ashoka**: Also known as Ashoka the Great, he succeeded Bindusara and is one of the most notable rulers of the Mauryan Empire. His reign (c. 268 BCE to 232 BCE) is marked by the spread of Buddhism and the issuance of the Edicts of Ashoka.
 
• **Samprati**: He was a Mauryan emperor and a successor of Ashoka. Although less known compared to Ashoka, Samprati is credited with continuing the promotion of Jainism during his reign.
 
• **Brihadratha**: He was the last ruler of the Mauryan Empire. His reign ended around 185 BCE when he was assassinated by his general Pushyamitra Shunga, who then established the Shunga dynasty.
 
• Thus, the correct order is **Bindusara → Ashoka → Samprati → Brihadratha**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Bindusara**__

 __
 
• He was known as **Amitraghata**, which means "Slayer of Enemies."
 
• Bindusara is said to have expanded the Mauryan Empire to cover most of the Indian subcontinent, except for parts of present-day Tamil Nadu and Kerala.
 
 
 
• **Ashoka**__
 __
 
• Under his reign, the Mauryan Empire reached its **greatest territorial extent.**
 
• Ashoka's transformation after the **Kalinga War** led him to adopt and promote **Buddhism**.
 
• He constructed numerous **stupas** and inscribed his policies in the form of the **Edicts of Ashoka**.
 
 
 
• **Samprati**__
 __
 
• He is believed to have built numerous **Jain temples** across India.
 
• Samprati is sometimes referred to as the "Jain Ashoka" due to his promotion of Jainism.
 
 
 
• **Brihadratha**__
 
 
• He was the last ruler of the Mauryan dynasty.
 
• His reign marked the **end of the Mauryan Empire**, which was succeeded by the Shunga dynasty.

questions.question: Who among the following Jain acharya was the spiritual teacher of Chandragupta Maurya, the founder of the Maurya Empire?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bhadrabahu**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bhadrabahu**

 
 
• **He was, according to the Digambara sect of Jainism, the last Shruta Kevalin in Jainism but Svetambara believes the last Shruta Kevalin was Acharya Sthulabhadra but was forbade by Bhadrabahu from disclosing it.**
 
• He was the last acharya of the undivided Jain sangha.
 
• **He was the spiritual teacher of Chandragupta Maurya, the founder of the Maurya Empire. Hence, Option 1 is correct.**
 
• According to the Digambara sect of Jainism, there were five Shruta Kevalins in Jainism - Govarddhana Mahamuni, Vishnu, Nandimitra, Aparajita, and Bhadrabahu.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hemchandra**

 
 
• He is the writer of 'Parishishtaparvan' is Acharya Hemchandra.
 
• According to the Parishishtaparvan, the earliest biography of Hemachandra, Jayasimha spotted Hemachandra while passing through the streets of his capital.
 
• The king was impressed with an impromptu verse uttered by the young monk
 
• Acharya Hemachandra was an Indian Jain scholar, poet, mathematician, and polymath who wrote on grammar, philosophy, prosody, mathematics, and contemporary history.
 
• Noted as a prodigy by his contemporaries, he gained the title kalikālasarvajña, "the knower of all knowledge in his times".
 
 
 
• **Siddhasena Divakara**
 
 
• **He was a Jain monk in the fifth century CE who wrote works on Jain philosophy and epistemology.**
 
• He was like the illuminating lamp of the Jain order and therefore came to be known as Divakara Lamp-Maker.
 
• He is credited with the authorship of many books, most of which are not available.
 
 
 
• Jinsen
 
 
• He was a monk and scholar in the Digambara tradition of Jainism.
 
• He was patronized by the Rashtrakuta king Amoghavarsha I.
 
• He was the author of Adipurana and Mahapurana.
 
• Jinasena was the disciple of Acharya Virasena and he completed the commentary Dhavala on Ṣaṭkhaṅḍāgama, a revered text in the Digambara tradition.
 
• The name is shared by an earlier Acharya Jinasena who was the author of Harivamsa Purana.

questions.question: The Mission of the Ramsar Convention is to conserve __________.
questions.solution:
**The Correct Answer is __Option 2__ i.e __wetlands__.**

 
• **Ramsar Convention:**

 
 
• The Ramsar Convention is an international treaty for the conservation and wise use of **wetlands**.
 
• It is named after the **Iranian city of Ramsar**, on the Caspian Sea, where the treaty was signed on 2 February 1971.
 
• it is also known as the wetlands convention.
 
• As of July 2021, there are 42 wetlands in India that have international importance and are hence recognized as the Ramsar Sites in India.
 
• The newly added 10 new Ramsar sites in India are:
 
 
• Maharashtra gets its first Ramsar site (Nandur Madhameshwar), Punjab which already had 3 Ramsar sites adds 3 more (Keshopur-Miani, Beas Conservation Reserve, Nangal) and UP with 1 Ramsar site has added 6 more (Nawabganj, Parvati Agra, Saman, Samaspur, Sandi and SarsaiNawar).
 
 
 
 
 
• United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS) provides the overarching framework for the governance of the oceans.

questions.question: In which year was the National Backward Classes Commission accorded constitutional status?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2018.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• The **National Backward Classes Commission** was given constitutional status through the **102nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 2018.**
 
• This Amendment has inserted new** Article 338B and 342A** in the Indian Constitution.
 
• **Article 338 B**:
 
 
• There will be a commission for **socially and educationally backward classes**, which will be known as **National Backward Classes Commission.**
 
• The commission will consist of a **chairman, deputy chairman, and three other members.**
 
• Their **terms of service and office** shall be such as shall be determined by the **President.**
 
• The** President** shall **appoint **the** Chairman, Deputy Chairman, and other members** of the Commission by warrant with his signature and seal.
 
• The Commission shall have the power to **self-regulate** its own procedure.
 
 
 
• **Article 342 A**:
 
 
• Under this, the **President** has been given the power to **mark** socially and educationally backward classes in various states and union territories.
 
• For this, the President can **consult** the Governor of the state concerned.
 
• But to amend the **Backward Class List**, legislation needs to be passed in **Parliament.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• **Historical Background**:

 
 
• According to** Article 340** of the Constitution of India, the **President of India** can appoint the **Commission **through an order to examine the conditions of **socially and educationally** backward classes and to provide recommendations related to improving their condition.
 
• Following Article 340 of the Constitution of India, the **First Backward Classes Commission** was established by **Presidential Order **on **29 January 1953** under the **chairmanship of Kaka Kelkar.**
 
 
• It is also known as the **First Backward Classes Commission** **1955** or **Kaka Kelkar Commission.**
 
• This commission** identified **the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes as well as other backward classes at the national level.
 
 
 
• The **Second Backward Classes Commission** was constituted in** 1979** under the chairmanship of **BP Mandal.**
 
 
• In the year** 1980**, the Commission submitted its report recommending** 27% reservation** in government jobs for backward classes.
 
 
 
• In the **Indira Sawhney case of 1992**, the Supreme Court recommended the government to set up a **statutory body** to protect the interests of backward classes.
 
• The **National Backward Classes Commission** was constituted by the Government of India on **14 August 1993 **under the National Backward Classes Commission Act on the direction of the Supreme Court. It was a **statutory body.**
 
• The main objective of the formation of this commission was to improve the condition of** socially and economically backward classes.**
 
• This Commission has reconstituted a total of **7 times** between **1993 and 2016.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **terms of service and conditions** are decided by the** President.**
 
• According to the rules, the tenure of the commission is **3 years.**
 
• The commission has the **powers **of the **civil court.**
 
• **Annual Report**:
 
 
• **Centre**: To President
 
• **State**: To Governor
 
 
 
• The present **Chairman of the Commission** is **Bhagwanlal Sahni.**

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the methods of national income estimation?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Banking method**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• National income is the total value of a country’s final output of all new goods and services produced in one year.
 
• Methods of measuring national income are:

 
• Expenditure Method - Under this method, we estimate the disposal of income on the purchase of final goods and services.
 
• Income Method - The Income Method measures national income from the side of payments made to the primary factors of production in the form of rent, wages, interest, and profit for their productive services in an accounting year. 
 
• Production method - In this method, national income is measured as a flow of goods and services. This method is also called an **output method**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• 
 Measurement of National Income

 
 
• 
 There are three methods to measure national income:

 
 
• **Income Method**
 
• **Production (Value-Added) Method**
 
• **Expenditure Method**
 
 
 
• 
 Measurement of National Income – Income Method

 
 
• Estimated by adding all the factors of production (rent, wages, interest, profit) and the mixed-income of self-employed.
 
• In India, one-third of people are self-employed
 
• This is the ‘**domestic**’ income, related to the production within the borders of the country
 
 
 
• Measurement of National Income – Production Method
 
 
• Estimated by adding the value added by all the firms.
 
• **Value-added** = Value of Output – Value of (non-factor) inputs
 

 
 
• This gives** GDP at Market Price (MP) – because it includes depreciation (therefore ‘gross’) and taxes (thus ‘market price’)**
 
• To reach National Income (that is, NNP at FC)
 

 
 
• Add Net Factor Income from Abroad: **GNP at MP = GDP at MP + NFIA**
 
• Subtract Depreciation:** NNP at MP = GNP at MP – Dep**
 
• Subtract Net Indirect Taxes: **NNP at FC = NNP at MP – NIT**
 
 
 
• Measurement of National Income – Expenditure Method
 
 
• The expenditure method to measure national income can be understood by the equation given below: 
 
 
• **Y = C + I + G + (X-M),**
 
• where** Y = GDP at MP, C = Private Sector’s Expenditure on final consumer goods, G = Govt’s expenditure on final consumer goods, I = Investment or Capital Formation, X = Exports, X- M = Net Exports (difference between exports (X) and imports (M))**
 
 
 
 
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] Important Points__**

 
• GDP: Gross Domestic Product is the sum of the money of all the final goods and services produced solely within the boundaries of a country, at a specific time.

 
 
• GDP includes the income of foreigners staying in the country.
 
• It excludes the income of nationals of the country staying abroad and also excludes the remittances sent from abroad.
 
 
 
• GNP: Gross National Product is the sum of the money of all the final goods and services produced both within and outside of a country by nationals during a specific period of time.
 
 
• GNP includes remittances.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an example of homogenous mixture?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Oil in water**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A homogenous mixture is a mixture that has the same uniform appearance and composition throughout.
 
• Examples of homogenous mixtures include solutions such as salt dissolved in water, sugar dissolved in water, and copper sulphate powder in water.
 
• Oil in water is not a homogenous mixture because oil and water do not mix evenly and form separate layers, making it a heterogeneous mixture.
 
• In a heterogeneous mixture, the components are not uniformly distributed and can often be easily separated.
 
• Homogenous mixtures have a single phase, whereas heterogeneous mixtures have two or more phases.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Solutions**

 
 
• These are homogenous mixtures where one substance (the solute) is dissolved in another substance (the solvent).
 
• Common examples include salt water and sugar water.
 
 
 
• **Suspensions**
 
 
• These are heterogeneous mixtures where solid particles do not dissolve but are suspended in a liquid or gas.
 
• Examples include sand in water or flour in water.
 
 
 
• **Colloids**
 
 
• These are mixtures where very small particles of one substance are evenly dispersed throughout another substance.
 
• Examples include milk, mayonnaise, and gelatin.
